elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: Inserted limb (b): "the Initial Development Activities and any other Development activities performed by Harpoon hereunder will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner."

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: Inserted limb (a): "any software and other deliverables provided by Harpoon to AbbVie hereunder will conform in all material respects to their documentation."

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: The insertion sets the conformance period at "ninety (90) days following delivery", not twelve months; to reach preferred the drafter must change "ninety (90) days" to "twelve (12) months".
The services/Development limb runs only "for thirty (30) days following performance"; preferred requires 90 days.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "Harpoon shall, at AbbVie's election, repair or replace the non-conforming deliverable, re-perform the non-conforming activities..."
"...or refund the amounts paid for them", preceded by a narrow override of the non-refundable language in Sections 6.1 through 6.4 so the refund leg is operative.

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: No warranty of legal compliance was added. Section 3.8.4 is a mutual performance covenant ("shall perform ... in compliance with all Applicable Law") with no warranty framing and no remedy; Sections 10.1/10.2 speak only "as of the Effective Date". Repair requires an express Harpoon warranty of compliance with Applicable Law covering its performance.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious-code (virus/disabling device) warranty appears anywhere in the retained text or the insertion.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: "(a) for ninety (90) days following delivery, any software and other deliverables provided by Harpoon to AbbVie hereunder will conform in all material respects to their documentation" — exactly the 90-day floor, expressly covering software.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: "(b) for thirty (30) days following performance, the Initial Development Activities and any other Development activities performed by Harpoon hereunder will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner" — 30-day floor with substantive performance content.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Remedy sentence expressly provides "repair or replace the non-conforming deliverable" (plus re-performance for activities).

"...or refund the amounts paid for them"; the opening "Notwithstanding any provision of this Agreement stating that payments are non-refundable, including Sections 6.1 through 6.4" prevents the retained non-refundable language from rendering the refund leg inoperative.

elements.element: Warranty survives the disclaimer in Section 10.5.
elements.evidence: Conditional/consequential check: 10.5 already opens "EXCEPT FOR THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES SET FORTH HEREIN", so the new warranty is carved out automatically and no edit to 10.5 was needed — correctly left untouched.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: 90-day software/deliverable conformance-to-documentation warranty, 30-day professional-and-workmanlike warranty for Harpoon's Development activities, and repair/replace, re-perform and refund remedies all appear in operative language, not merely in the comment.

Preferred is not reached and the comment correctly says so: the software period is 90 days rather than 12 months, the services period is 30 days rather than 90 days, and there is no compliance-with-laws warranty or malicious-code warranty. To move to preferred the drafter must (i) change "ninety (90) days" to "twelve (12) months", (ii) change "thirty (30) days" to "ninety (90) days", (iii) add an express Harpoon warranty that its performance complies with Applicable Law (Section 3.8.4 is a covenant, not a warranty, and carries no remedy), and (iv) add a no-malicious-code warranty.

The insertion is a concise new clause for a missing warranty, so wholly new wording is acceptable; it adds no survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no notice procedure and no extra damages categories, and it leaves Sections 10.1, 10.2 and 10.5 untouched.

The narrow non-refundable override is justified by necessity rather than an extra: without it the retained "non-refundable, non-creditable" language in Section 6.1 (and 6.2-6.4) would contradict the refund element, so intent is preserved rather than disturbed. Confirm before sending that Sections 6.2 through 6.4 in fact contain the non-refundable payment mechanics, otherwise narrow the cite to avoid a dangling cross-reference.

Negotiation note (not a defect against the checklist): the remedy is framed "at AbbVie's election" whereas playbook model language puts the choice at Vendor's option; if Harpoon pushes back, conceding "at Harpoon's option" still satisfies every fallback element.
